title: Per-request residency budgeting and preemptible KV residency to meet tail-latency SLAs
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background:
Redwood's paged/blocked KV cache has made great progress on reducing OOMs and improving steady-state throughput, but we still observe episodic tail-latency spikes for latency-sensitive routes when large multiplexer requests compete for limited GPU residency. Continuous batching amplifies the problem: a batched request with mixed residency needs can force long-running prefetches and eviction churn that push latency over our SLA.

Problem statement:
We need a schema for per-request residency budgeting and a runtime mechanism for marking some KV pages as preemptible so that: 1) latency-sensitive requests can obtain a bounded amount of resident KV memory; 2) long-running background prefetches or batch-head requests cannot monopolize GPU residency; and 3) eviction/proactive compaction behavior cooperates with the batch scheduler to preserve tail-latency SLOs.

Goals:
- Define a per-request residency budget concept exposed to the scheduler and serving runtime.
- Implement preemptible residency flags and fast preemption path for eviction under latency pressure.
- Integrate budgeting with continuous-batching policies so that the batcher can split or prioritize work when budgets are insufficient.
- Keep CPU-GPU sync costs low; avoid per-token GPU synchronizations for accounting.
- Provide observability and a graceful rollout with feature flagging for dedicated capacity customers.
acceptance_criteria:
- Residency budgets accepted by scheduler: requests can attach budget metadata and the plan is exercised in unit/integration tests.
- Preemptible residency implemented: pages marked preemptible are evicted within the configured SLO under pressure (bench confirms eviction latency < 2ms median, 99th < 10ms).
- Batcher integration: when budgets cannot be honored, batcher either breaks batches or reorders low-priority requests to avoid SLA violations (demonstrated in load test harness).
- No regression on throughput: under steady-state throughput tests we should be within 5% of baseline for P50 latency and token/sec.
- Telemetry: new metrics emitted (per-request budget, preempted_pages, preemption_latency, budget_violation_count) and dashboards created for runtime-1.20 rollout.
tasks: Design budget schema and API for request envelope (proto/REST header)
Add residency bookkeeping: lightweight per-request counters in CPU-side scheduler
Mark pages as preemptible at allocation time (allocation flags + stamp)
Implement fast GPU preemption path: async eviction list + kernel-friendly free list
Batcher changes: budget-aware batch formation and fallback strategies
Load tests with mixed high/low priority routes (compare baseline)
Feature-flag rollout to canary then Dedicated pools
design_decisions:
- Budget unit chosen: resident_slots (approx 4KB slot size) to avoid per-token bookkeeping.
- Preemptible vs pinned pages: pages allocated in response to low-priority or prefetches default to preemptible; model activation KV slots for foreground requests are pinned until budget expiry or explicit release.
- Accounting scope: budgets are enforced at request-level and aggregated at device-level; the scheduler maintains a fast approximate counter for available_slots to avoid atomic contention.
- Preemption policy: LRU-variant with token-recentness + request-priority score; pages with preemptible flag and low recency evicted first.
- Avoid per-token GPU synchronization: preemption issues an async free list that is drained by the next kernel launch or during idle compaction windows.
- Batcher interaction: when a proposal batch would exceed device budget headroom, the batcher will either (a) split the batch into budget-conforming chunks, or (b) postpone low-priority queued requests and continue with high-priority ones.
- Fallback: if preemption cannot free enough slots in time, runtime falls back to a compatible smaller model variant (if configured) to preserve latency SLOs.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): runtime binary with flags enabled in internal test cluster; traffic seeded with synthetic mixes.
Phase 2 (beta): enable for 10% of Dedicated pools with monitoring and automatic rollback on budget_violation_count spike.
Phase 3 (general): enable for selected latency-sensitive routes in hosted tier, with conservative default budgets and opt-in via route config.
All phases: toggle to disable preemption on a per-pool basis and config knobs for budget size, preemption aggressiveness, and compaction window length.
monitoring:
Emit metrics: runtime.residency.available_slots, runtime.residency.request_budget_requested, runtime.residency.request_budget_used, runtime.residency.preempted_pages, runtime.residency.preemption_latency_ms, runtime.residency.compaction_time_ms.
Create Grafana dashboard: per-device and per-route view.
Alerting: page on sustained budget_violation_count > threshold for 5m, and warn on preemption_latency P99 > 50ms.
